title: Why a US AI company is building a giant computer hub in Navi Mumbai
subtitle: CoreWeave plans 240 MW of AI data centres near Mumbai, with room to double. Here is what that means, explained simply.
content_html:
Picture this. You type a question into an AI app, and in moments an answer appears. That answer did not come from your phone. It came from a giant building full of powerful computers. On 6 October 2026, an American company called CoreWeave said it will build that kind of building, in fact three of them, in Navi Mumbai.

The plan is big: 240 MW of data centre space, with a chance to double it later. Here is what all of that means, in simple words.

What is a data centre?

A data centre is a huge building packed with computers that run day and night. Think of it like the kitchen behind a food delivery app. You only see the app, but the real cooking happens in a big kitchen far away.

AI apps work the same way. Your question travels to a data centre, special chips there do the heavy maths, and the answer travels back to your screen.

The special chips are called GPUs. A normal computer chip is like one very smart student solving sums one by one. A GPU is like a whole classroom solving lots of small sums at the same time. AI needs exactly that kind of teamwork.

Who is CoreWeave?

CoreWeave calls itself "The Essential Cloud for AI". It started in 2017 and its shares began trading on the Nasdaq stock market in the US in March 2025.

What does a cloud company do? It rents out computers. Imagine you want to play a cricket match. You do not build your own stadium. You rent a ground by the hour. AI companies do the same with CoreWeave: they rent its GPUs instead of buying their own. People call cloud companies like this, built mainly for AI, "neoclouds", which simply means new clouds.

Here is a CoreWeave video about the AI data centres behind its cloud.

What exactly is coming to Navi Mumbai?

CoreWeave is teaming up with AdaniConneX, a data centre company that is a 50:50 joint venture between Adani Enterprises and EdgeConneX. A joint venture is when two companies start something together and share it, like two friends who each put in half the money for one lemonade stall.

Here is the plan, according to CoreWeave:

  • Where: AdaniConneX's Taloja campus in Navi Mumbai.
  • How big: 240 MW across three buildings of 80 MW each.
  • Who uses it: CoreWeave will be the only tenant, meaning the only renter, in all three buildings.
  • When: The first phase should be ready by mid-2028, with more space coming in steps after that.
  • Room to grow: CoreWeave has the option to add up to another 240 MW at the same campus.
  • Chips: It plans to use NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform.
  • Jobs: It plans to open an office in India and hire people locally.

Wait, what does 240 MW mean?

Data centres are measured by how much electricity they can use, not by how many floors they have. Electricity is measured in watts. Mega means million, so one megawatt (MW) is a million watts. More megawatts means room for more computers.

Here is a way to feel the size. Over the past three decades, India built about 2.2 GW of working data centre capacity. A GW, or gigawatt, is 1,000 MW, so that is about 2,200 MW. CoreWeave's 240 MW alone is more than a tenth of that. If it uses its option and reaches 480 MW, it would be more than a fifth.

And the race is only starting. A Wood Mackenzie report from July expects India to reach 12 GW by 2030, with AI capacity growing almost 24 times to 6.5 GW.

How much money is this?

CoreWeave did not share a number. Bloomberg reported the investment will be multiple billions of dollars over the life of the project.

Why India?

CoreWeave's Chief Operating Officer, Sachin Jain, said: "India has the talent, developers, and ambition to become a major center of AI innovation."

There are a few more clues:

  • Demand: CoreWeave's CEO Mike Intrator said in September that the company is "largely sold out" of space, according to Bloomberg. When every table in your restaurant is full, you open a new branch.
  • Asia plan: India is CoreWeave's second market in Asia. In August it announced its first data centre projects in Indonesia.
  • Government push: The company linked this move to the government's IndiaAI Mission.

Keeping the computers cool

Ever noticed your phone getting hot after a long game? GPUs get hot too. These buildings will use direct liquid cooling, where cold liquid flows close to the chips to carry the heat away. They will also use a chilled water system that does not depend on water evaporating.

Not the only big build

CoreWeave is not alone. AdaniConneX also teamed up with Google in October 2025 on an AI data centre campus in Visakhapatnam, part of Google's 15 billion dollar investment.

So, why should you care?

  • Faster AI nearby: When the computers sit closer to users, answers can travel a shorter distance.
  • Local jobs: CoreWeave plans to open an office in India and hire people here.
  • A long game: The first phase is expected only by mid-2028, so this is a plan for the next few years, not next week.

The next time an AI app answers you in a flash, remember the giant, humming, carefully cooled building behind it. Soon, a few of those could be in Navi Mumbai.
